candidates.title: In Japan, Light Rain Goes "Shito Shito" 🌧️ #japan #shorts
candidates.description:
In Japan, light rain goes "shito shito"... and heavy rain goes "zaa zaa"! 🌧️

🌦️ Light rain: shito shito (シトシト) 🌧️ Heavy rain: zaa zaa (ザーザー) 💧 A raindrop: pichon (ピチョン) 🌬️ Strong wind: byuu byuu (ビュービュー) ☀️ Blazing sun: gira gira (ギラギラ) 🌊 A big wave: zabaan (ザブーン) ❄️ Falling snow: shin shin (シンシン) 👢 A puddle: picha picha (ピチャピチャ) ⛈️ Thunder: goro goro (ゴロゴロ) ⚡ Lightning: pika! (ピカッ)

English has no sound for falling snow or a blazing sun, but Japanese does. "Shin shin" is the sound of silent, steady snow.

Fun fact: "pika" is the flash of light, the same "pika" said to be in Pikachu's name. ⚡

candidates.description:
Follow for a new health or science clip every day ⚡

If you shake a sleeping person, they wake up — they can reclaim their consciousness. If you shake a person in a coma or someone under general anesthesia, they don't. That reversibility is the single most important word in the scientific definition of sleep, because it proves sleep is a dynamic, active state the brain can exit on command if the stimulus is strong enough. Which makes sleep a suspension of consciousness, not a loss of it.

candidates.description:
Spinal nerves are the peripheral nerves that emerge from the spinal cord and carry both sensory and motor information.
In this Short you’ll see:
Anterior (ventral) root – pure motor
Posterior (dorsal) root – pure sensory
Spinal (dorsal root) ganglion – sensory cell bodies
Spinal nerve – mixed nerve (31 pairs)
Posterior ramus – back muscles & skin
Anterior ramus – limbs & trunk
Key takeaway:
Lesion of the posterior root → pure sensory loss (dermatome)
Lesion of the anterior root → pure motor loss (myotome)
Lesion of the spinal nerve or rami → mixed deficit

candidates.title: Which Ball Wins? The Answer Breaks Your Intuition #shorts
candidates.description:
Two balls start at the same point and finish at the same point. One rolls down a straight ramp, the shortest path. The other takes a longer curve that even dips below the finish. Which one arrives first?

The curve wins by almost a full second. A ball's speed depends only on how far it has dropped, and the curve drops steeply right at the start, so its ball is nearly three times as fast after one second.

This fastest curve is called the brachistochrone, Greek for "shortest time". Did you guess right? Tell me in the comments.

1. Hello — こんにちは (Konnichiwa)
2. Thank you — ありがとうございます (Arigatou gozaimasu)
3. Excuse me — すみません (Sumimasen)

5. What is it? — なんですか？ (Nan desu ka?)

candidates.title: In Japanese, Sun + Moon = ? ☀️🌙 #japan #kanji  #shorts
candidates.description:
In Japanese, sun + moon = ... bright? ☀️🌙

Many kanji are built from smaller kanji:

☀️ 日 (sun) + 🌙 月 (moon) = 明 → bright (akarui)
🌳 木 (tree) + 木 (tree) = 林 → woods (hayashi)
🌲 木 + 木 + 木 (three trees) = 森 → forest (mori)
😴 人 (person) + 木 (tree) = 休 → rest (yasumu)
💪 田 (field) + 力 (power) = 男 → man (otoko)
🐦 口 (mouth) + 鳥 (bird) = 鳴 → chirp (naku)
🔥 火 (fire) + 火 (fire) = 炎 → flame (honoo)

These are popular ways to remember the kanji. The real history of some characters is a little different.

Which kanji would you build? 👇

#Japan #LearnJapanese #Shorts

candidates.title: 🇯🇵 Japanese Yōon Explained! きゃ・しゅ・ちょ | Learn Japanese #japanese #hiragana
candidates.description:
🇯🇵 Learn Japanese Yōon (拗音) | Small ゃ・ゅ・ょ Explained

Did you know that two Hiragana characters can combine to create one blended sound?

In this beginner-friendly Japanese lesson, learn how Yōon (拗音) works and how small ゃ, ゅ, and ょ change the pronunciation.

📚 What is Yōon?

Yōon (拗音) is a combination of an I-row Hiragana character with a small ゃ, ゅ, or ょ.

✨ Examples:

き + ゃ = きゃ (kya)
し + ゅ = しゅ (shu)
ち + ょ = ちょ (cho)

⚠️ Important difference:

❌ きや = kiya (two separate sounds)
✅ きゃ = kya (blended sound)

Remember: The second character must be SMALL and written at the bottom right.

candidates.title: Why the first second always feels longer #science #neuroscience #explained
candidates.description:
Look at a clock with a second hand. That first second always seems to hang there a beat too long.

👁️ Getting your eyes to the clock takes a saccade — a fast jump — and your brain turns the picture down while your eyes are moving. That leaves a gap of missing footage.

🕐 Rather than show you the gap, your brain backdates the first thing you land on and fills the missing interval with it. So the stretched second isn't your imagination: you really were shown that image for longer than a second.

Could you have survived it?

Everyone calls e^(iπ) + 1 = 0 the strangest equation in math — until you see what multiplying by i actually does on the complex plane.

Instead of stretching numbers forward like e^x, putting i in the exponent turns your velocity 90° sideways so you glide smoothly around the unit circle. Walk π radians (half a turn), land on -1, add 1, and you return straight to 0.

candidates.description:
Forget memorizing det(A - λI) = 0! What is an eigenvector in real life? 🧭⚡

When a matrix transforms space, almost EVERY vector gets rotated and knocked off its original span line.

Except for very special directions: EIGENVECTORS! 🎯

1️⃣ While the rest of space spins or shears, an eigenvector stays LOCKED on its exact same span line. It refuses to turn!
2️⃣ The only thing that happens to it is stretching or shrinking.
3️⃣ The scale factor of that stretch? That is the EIGENVALUE (λ)! If λ = 2.0, the vector simply doubles in length without changing its direction.

✅ Star: every device connects to a central switch (the most common layout today)
✅ Ring: each device connects to two neighbors, and data travels around the circle
✅ Mesh: many connections, so data can take another path (very reliable, but costs more)
✅ Tree: stars connected in a hierarchy
✅ Hybrid: a mix of different topologies
